contentBlocks.text: ਅੱਜ ਪਹਿਲਾ ਮੁਹਾਵਰਾ! (Today, the first idiom!) A well-known Punjabi idiom about making a bad situation worse.

The idiom is ਅੱਗ ਵਿੱਚ ਘਿਓ ਪਾਉਣਾ (agg vich ghio pauna). Literally, this means 'to pour ghee into fire' — new words: ਅੱਗ (agg, fire) and ਘਿਓ (ghio, ghee, a type of clarified butter). Since ghee is very flammable, pouring it on a fire makes the fire much bigger and worse. The real meaning: to make an already-bad situation even worse, often by saying or doing the wrong thing at the wrong moment — very similar to the English idiom 'adding fuel to the fire.' Think of an example situation (real or made-up) where someone's comment or action would count as 'pouring ghee into fire.'
You just learned a real, commonly used Punjabi idiom, its literal meaning, and its actual meaning. Tomorrow we'll learn a second idiom, about finding the truth.

objectives: Learn the idiom ਅੱਗ ਵਿੱਚ ਘਿਓ ਪਾਉਣਾ, its literal meaning, and its real meaning
Apply the idiom to a real or invented example situation
teacherGuide.facilitationScript:
1. Review yesterday's idiom concept.
2. Introduce today's idiom, its literal words (ਅੱਗ/ਘਿਓ), and its real meaning.
3. Compare it to the English 'adding fuel to the fire.'
4. Have the child think of an example situation where this idiom would apply.
5. Complete the worksheet.
6. Preview tomorrow's topic: a second idiom.
differentiationTips: Struggling: focus on just recognizing and translating the idiom, without requiring an original example situation yet
Ready for more: ask them why ghee specifically (rather than water or oil) makes this idiom work so well (it's highly flammable)
All Gurmukhi words/phrases used in this lesson were validated against gurmukhifix's Lexicon before writing
teacherGuide.answerKey: 1. Literal meaning: to pour ghee into fire. 2. Real meaning: to make a bad situation worse. 3. Answers will vary for the child's own example situation.
teacherGuide.standardsRationale: Teaches the course's first named real idiom with complete literal-vs-real meaning analysis, matching the 'common idioms' description with a genuine, well-known example rather than an invented one.
